name: EWE

paper.title: Improving Factuality with Explicit Working Memory

construction.unit: memory unit: the KV cache of one M-token text chunk (a retrieved passage or fact-check evidence)
construction.kept_as: verbatim passages, stored as KV caches rather than text
construction.processing: at pauses, retrieved passages above a score threshold and evidence for unsupported claims are each encoded separately by the generator into KV caches with shared position ids
construction.writer: the generator LLM (Llama-3.1 70B/8B) encodes; Contriever retrieves; VeriScore's claim extractor and verifier supply evidence

organization.structure: k parallel memory units, kept separately for retrieval feedback and fact-check feedback
organization.stores: working memory of KV caches outside the prompt, prepended per layer
organization.index: none inside memory; external datastore searched with Contriever (C4 + Wikipedia, MassiveDS)

management.operations: new units replace old ones first in, first out; a sentence with unsupported claims is deleted and regenerated
management.conflicts: fact-check evidence for refuted claims enters memory before the sentence is rewritten
management.forgetting: FIFO eviction when a pool is full

retrieval.query: input question + the sentence being checked
retrieval.candidates: Contriever dense search over C4 + Wikipedia; Google snippets inside the fact-checker
retrieval.selection: passages whose retrieval score passes a threshold
retrieval.budget: k units × M tokens; the values used for the main table are not stated (sweeps: 1-50 units, 128-6,400 tokens)

use.context: each memory unit is concatenated with the context in a separate attention pass per layer, plus one context-only pass; outputs are averaged with weights from the attention normalisers
use.reasoning: sentence-by-sentence decoding with pauses, checks and backtracking

classify.note: Two FIFO pools (retrieval feedback, fact-check feedback) of KV-cache units; admission is a retrieval-score threshold rather than a fixed k.

stages.ingestion: Decoding pauses periodically (retrieval every Tr=1 and verification every Tv=8 timesteps in the main runs); a pause does nothing unless a new sentence is complete.
stages.construction: Passages retrieved with the question and the new sentence as query (score above a threshold) and, when VeriScore finds unsupported claims, the evidence passages are each encoded by the generator into a separate KV-cache unit of M tokens.
stages.organization: Units sit in a working memory outside the prompt, with retrieval feedback and fact-check feedback kept apart; all units share the same position ids.
stages.update: Pools are refreshed first in, first out; a sentence with false claims is removed and generation backs up to regenerate it with the new units.
stages.retrieval: Contriever over C4 + Wikipedia (MassiveDS), query = question + current sentence, filtered by a score threshold.
stages.answer: At every layer each unit is attended together with the context in parallel, plus a context-only pass, and the hidden vectors are averaged using the attention normalisers (Eq. 1).

summary: Long-form generation with a working memory of KV-cached passages that is refreshed during decoding from retrieval and online fact-checking, with backtracking when a sentence is found false.
notes:
Venue: ACL 2025 long paper (aclanthology 2025.acl-long.548); arXiv comment 'ACL 2025 Camera Ready'. PDF read: arXiv v3 (2 Jun 2025). No code link in the paper, the ACL page or a GitHub search. Abstract v3 says +2 to 6 VeriScore points.
DESIGN: §1, §3.1-3.2, §4, App. B-D. Memory here is per-generation working memory for factual long-form answers, not memory across sessions.

sources.code_note: No official code found (not linked in the paper or the ACL Anthology page; GitHub search found nothing). Everything below is from the paper; the number and length of memory units and the retrieval threshold used for Table 1 are not given.

headline: Memory is a set of KV caches of passages, read by the model's attention in parallel passes, not text pasted into the prompt.
The same VeriScore claim extractor and verifier that feed the memory at inference are used to score the outputs.

units.name: Memory unit
units.role: one chunk of feedback text, cached
units.made_by: the generator LLM encoding the chunk separately

fields.name: retrieved passage
fields.what: Contriever passage from C4 or Wikipedia, kept if its score passes a threshold

fields.name: fact-check evidence
fields.what: passages VeriScore used to judge a claim (supporting passages performed best; Table 4)

fields.name: KV cache
fields.what: the unit's keys and values at every layer, all units sharing the same position ids

write.how: stop decoding at fixed intervals; skip if no new complete sentence
Contriever search of C4 + Wikipedia with question + current sentence; keep passages above a score threshold

params.threshold: not stated for Table 1 (1.5-2.2 swept, Fig. 5)

write.how: VeriScore extracts claims from the sentence and verifies them against Google snippets; evidence for unsupported claims becomes feedback
each feedback chunk is run through the generator separately to produce its KV cache
insert new units, evicting the oldest first (FIFO); other rules tried did no better

read.scores: each memory unit concatenated with the context
read.how: standard self-attention per unit plus a context-only pass; hidden vectors averaged with weights from the attention normalisers (Eq. 1)
if any claim is unsupported, delete the sentence and regenerate from the previous step with the refreshed memory

answer_context.sees: prompt and generated text as context, plus every memory unit through the parallel attention passes
answer_context.format: memory units are not text in the prompt; they act as per-layer KV prefixes
excludes: retrieved passages under the score threshold

compression.basis: Not reported: the unit count and length used in the main runs are not stated.

open_questions: The number and length of memory units and the retrieval threshold for Table 1 are not given, and the sweeps in Fig. 3-5 are on 50 LongFact prompts.
Fact-checking at inference and scoring use the same VeriScore models; the human check (Table 2) covers 100 samples per system.

ablation.src: paper Table 4 (VeriScore on 50 LongFact prompts, Llama-3.1-70B)

components.model: VeriScore fine-tuned claim extractor and verifier, Google snippets

discussion.takeaway: Giving the generator a refreshable working memory of cached passages, fed by retrieval and an online fact-checker, raises factuality of long answers over RAG and iterative-retrieval baselines without making them less helpful.

claims.claim: Best factuality on all four datasets.
claims.evidence: VeriScore F1 with Llama-3.1-70B: 75.9 / 61.0 / 66.9 / 49.7 on LongFact / Fava / AlpacaFact / Biography vs best baseline 72.7 / 57.2 / 66.0 / 43.8. Table 1
AlpacaEval win rate vs the 70B base: 49.9-50.2 for EWE-70B, all other 70B methods 9.1-49.4. Table 1

claims.claim: Gains are smaller with the 8B model.
Too many or too short units hurt; unit length trades precision for recall.

claims.evidence: F1 74.8 with both passage types vs 72.5 with instructions only. Table 4

claims.claim: The datastore matters and preferences differ by dataset.
claims.evidence: LongFact 67.9 Wiki / 70.8 C4 / 74.8 both; Biography 46.1 / 44.6 / 48.4. Table 3

limits: Only English fact-seeking prompts were tested.
Only textual feedback; multimodal feedback not explored.
reading: The fact-checker used during generation is VeriScore's own claim extractor and verifier, and the metric is VeriScore F1, so part of the gain may come from optimising against the evaluator; the human study (κ 0.65 vs 0.61 on 100 samples each) only checks that VeriScore still agrees with people.
Over plain RA the 70B gains are 3.2 / 4.2 / 0.9 / 5.9 F1; on AlpacaFact the gain is under one point.
Memory size (units, unit length) and the retrieval threshold for the main table are not reported; all sweeps use 50 LongFact prompts with the 70B model.
Even with no feedback text, pausing and regenerating flagged sentences reaches 73.0 F1 vs 72.5 for RA (Table 4), so the checker's trigger alone accounts for part of the effect.
Baselines use the same retriever and datastore, but Nest uses 100 candidate passages and RA 10; CoVe was adapted from a third-party implementation.
Biography has 181 prompts in §4.1 but 183 names in App. A.

abstract.text: EWE adds an explicit working memory to an LLM that writes long factual answers. The memory holds KV caches of passages; while generating, the model pauses, retrieves passages for the latest sentence, and runs a fact-checker whose evidence also enters memory. Sentences found false are deleted and rewritten with the refreshed memory. On four fact-seeking long-form datasets the method raises VeriScore by 2-6 points with Llama-3.1 without lowering AlpacaEval helpfulness, and the analysis points to memory update rules, unit configuration and datastore quality as the key factors.
